Thanks Marissa — appreciate the quick kickoff. Attached our initial requirements spreadsheet (MAP tab) and a note on target SLOs. High level: for our production workload (batched inference for user personalization) we need
- P99 latency <= 220ms for 512-token requests at 8 concurrent streams
- TTFT (time to first token) <= 35ms on average for chat-style calls
- Sustained throughput ~7,500 tokens/sec during batch windows

We want clear pass/fail gating per environment (hosted / dedicated / private) and explicit autoscale behavior during 2x-4x traffic bursts. Can Redwood run the standard comparator and give raw logs?

-Mike
Skyline Analytics

Thanks Mike — attaching our proposed MAP (MAP_Skyline_v1.xlsx) with an evaluation plan and gating criteria. Quick callouts before we schedule the lab run next Tue:
- Test matrix: three environments (Hosted API, Dedicated pool, Private VPC). For each we will run: steady-state (baseline), 2x spike, 4x spike, and long-tail isolation run (no co-tenants)
- Metrics captured: P50/P95/P99 latency, TTFT median and 95th, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, and KV cache hit-rate
- Autoscale policy used: default scaling for Hosted, committed nodes for Dedicated with burst to 1.5x, and customer-configured autoscale for Private (we will test both conservative and aggressive profiles)

Can you confirm test window (we proposed Mon 04/05 01:00–04:00 UTC) and supply two sample payloads (chat short ~64 tokens, batch long ~512 tokens)?

I'll loop in Rishi for any contract gating we need to include in the MAP and Karthik/Tessa for infra/test ownership.

Best,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — perf gating and hosting tests

We ran the first lab yesterday against the three hosting modes (see perf_logs_20270401.tar.gz). Summary highlights (short):
- Hosted API: predictable P50/P95, but P99 had occasional spikes up to 380ms under 4x burst due to multi-tenant cold-paths. TTFT median 28ms, 95th 60ms. Autoscale latency-to-add-node ~45s in our controlled burst test.
- Dedicated: much tighter P99 tail (P99 <= 210ms) when nodes were isolated. With committed baseline + 1.5x burst option, TTFT median 32ms, 95th 45ms. Queue depth stayed low, GPU util plateaued ~78% under steady-state.
- Private (VPC): behavior depended heavily on customer autoscale profile. Under aggressive autoscale we matched Dedicated P99 and throughput; under conservative profile we observed P99 up to 420ms due to delayed node provisioning and cold-starts.

Notable failure mode: Hosted showed prefix cache invalidation during a contiguous 18-minute window (we saw KV cache hit-rate drop from 88% to 42%), which correlated with P99 spikes. logs include span traces and request ids.

Proposed MAP gating: Pass if P99 <= 250ms and TTFT 95th <= 80ms for the baseline and 2x spike tests; for 4x spike mark as conditional pass with recommended mitigations (increase dedicated baseline or tune autoscale).

Will drop a short technical note into the Drive and propose a reconciliation call.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — very helpful. A few clarifying questions from our infra team: 
1) For Hosted, can you confirm whether the cache invalidation was customer-scope (affecting only Skyline) or cross-tenant housekeeping?
2) For Private, what tuning knobs do you recommend for the conservative autoscale profile so we avoid cold-start P99s?

We're trying to finalize the mutual action plan and the procurement timeline. Our target close is week of 04/19 — is that realistic if we get an updated MAP and a remediation plan for the Hosted spikes?

-Mike
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mike Ross <mike@skyline-analytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — perf gating and hosting tests

Mike — quick answers and next steps: 
- Cache invalidation: investigation shows the Hosted spike was cross-tenant housekeeping on the shard that handled your traffic; not Skyline-specific. We have a remediation: patch to reduce aggressive GC windows + route affinity option for customers (we can enable route affinity for your tenant during the pilot).
- Private tuning: recommend a two-stage autoscale: (1) conservative baseline buffer (reserve 10% extra nodes during known batch windows), (2) predictive warmers (pre-provision nodes 30s before scheduled batch start using a simple cron-based signal). Together these reduced cold-start P99s in our lab to ~180–220ms in prior customers.

MAP + close timeline: we will: 1) circulate MAP_Skyline_v1 with gating language updated (P99 pass threshold 250ms; conditional pass for 4x spike) by EOD Wed 04/07; 2) deliver remediation plan for Hosted spikes (engineering note + optional route affinity) by Thu 04/08; 3) run a final verification window Mon 04/12 with you. If verification passes, commercial can circulate contract by Tue 04/13 and target signature close week of 04/19 as requested.

Action items for you: confirm test payloads and approve the verification window.

Thanks — Marissa
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
